_meta.note: Team ceiling = team hours / (team hours - hours freed). Smaller team keeps half-FTE steps per role. Pods group every task by value stream (keyword rules on the task statement, then the role default).

teams.name: HR
teams.north_star: Share of open roles filled with a hire who is productive and still here after 90 days
value_streams: absence to return (verzuim, Wet verbetering poortwachter)
teams.ceiling_explained: The team spends 31% of its 20,800 hours on human tasks that stay at today's speed. With the models' median speedups it gets 1.3x faster (4,985 hours, 3.1 FTE a year). The hard limit is 3.3x: approval gates and handoffs inside the AI tasks already sit in the models' speedups, so this is the ceiling before the work itself is redesigned.

ambitious.label: Same team, more ambitious work (Jevons)
ambitious.text: Keep all 13 people. The 4,985 hours a year that come back (3.1 FTE, EUR 337,631 of loaded cost) go to work that was never done properly, moving the North Star: share of open roles filled with a hire who is productive and still here after 90 days.

by_role.title: HR Administrator
by_role.ambitious_version: The desk answers all three sites on the same day, including the night shift. Overnight warehouse applications are checked against the vacancy before the shift lead arrives. Eligible floor staff hear about an internal vacancy inside the CAO window. A shift worker can get a quoted allowance answer, and a same-day employer statement, without calling Rotterdam in the morning. Supervisors see certificate expiry in time to book the course. Flex workers get a short sheet of what applies to them and what stays with the agency. The administrators keep those tables and wording current with the works council, and the recruiters, HR Business Partners, and Compensation and Benefits see the exceptions and the day-90 result.

by_role.title: Learning and Development Specialist
by_role.ambitious_version: Every new hire and every flex worker is certified before the first shift, on day and night shift, at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, and the week-one onboarding record matches what happened. Warehouse leads at Tilburg and Venlo have a path toward team lead that the HR Director sponsors. The specialists can show the works council one file on what the company has done for AI literacy under Article 4. The figures they report are first-shift certification, week-one onboarding and who is still productive at day 90.

by_role.title: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
by_role.ambitious_version: Noordhaven runs one workforce measurement standard for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, for day and night, and for employees and flex workers. On the second working day the HR Director sees 90-day retention and the verzuim rate and duration, tied to AFAS, with a sourced note on what moved. The Controller sees the same FTE on the finance calendar. Compensation and Benefits sees a labour-market comparison before a pay decision. The works council can read what is measured and what is excluded. The analyst's week is the standard, the failed checks and the exceptions. Individual scores for attrition or absence stay outside that ambition.

by_role.title: Payroll Specialist
by_role.ambitious_version: Provide a payroll reliability service across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: first-pay readiness for new hires, early detection of payment and pension failures, reconciled cost information for Finance, and accessible form intake for night shifts. Measure first-time-right pay, corrections per run and first-pay failures alongside the HR North Star, and test whether fewer pay problems improve 90-day retention. Expand through supported AFAS rules and bounded document intake, using the released capacity for difficult employee cases and prevention.

by_role.title: Recruiter (talent acquisition)
by_role.ambitious_version: The recruiter runs one pipeline for fixed hires and agency flex workers across three sites, reports monthly which criteria and sources predict 90-day retention, and steers agency spend with Finance.

by_role.title: HR Business Partner
by_role.ambitious_version: The three HRBPs provide a coordinated service across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: accessible policy guidance, shift-compatible manager coaching and a monthly hire-to-day-90 improvement clinic. They use released capacity to improve week-one onboarding and successful 90-day outcomes, measuring questions resolved without HRBP intervention, days from issue raised to resolution, manager satisfaction and whether workers trust the service.

by_role.title: Compensation and Benefits Specialist
by_role.ambitious_version: One job architecture covers the three sites. Recruiters publish a band that already exists. HR business partners get a yes or no on a new title without inventing a scale. The works council sees unexplained gaps, including agency workers when the agencies supply pay, in time to act before a statutory report. Night-shift team leads hear the same pay rules as the office. The specialist's week is disputed jobs, CAO changes and those conversations.

by_role.title: HR Director
by_role.ambitious_version: Run an integrated hire-to-day-90 service for operations at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo, covering permanent hires and flex workers where agency agreements permit. Use monthly workforce decisions, coordinated onboarding and certificate plans, and site intervention reviews to improve the share of hires who are productive and still present at day 90, while the director retains consequential decisions and the OR participates in applicable changes.

smaller.label: Smaller team, same output
smaller.text: The same output needs 9.9 FTE of work. Kept in half-FTE steps per role that is 12 FTE instead of 13, through natural turnover rather than dismissals. One-person roles keep at least half an FTE and need cover for holidays and absence.

pods.label: Polyvalent pods per value stream
pods.text: Instead of functional roles, one small pod owns each value stream end to end and covers its tasks across today's roles; each person takes the adjacent tasks that the models' reach lines point to.

teams.name: Finance
teams.north_star: Days to close the month with a forecast the business trusts
teams.ceiling_explained: The team spends 27% of its 16,000 hours on human tasks that stay at today's speed. With the models' median speedups it gets 1.6x faster (5,717 hours, 3.6 FTE a year). The hard limit is 3.7x: approval gates and handoffs inside the AI tasks already sit in the models' speedups, so this is the ceiling before the work itself is redesigned.

ambitious.label: Same team, more ambitious work (Jevons)
ambitious.text: Keep all 10 people. The 5,717 hours a year that come back (3.6 FTE, EUR 378,382 of loaded cost) go to work that was never done properly, moving the North Star: days to close the month with a forecast the business trusts.

by_role.title: Bookkeeper (accounts payable and receivable)
by_role.ambitious_version: Provide a shared early-warning service for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: unresolved cash items each working day, emerging ledger discrepancies during the month, and weekly views of commitments and company-owned stock issues. Prioritise exceptions by their effect on close readiness and forecast reliability, then measure days to close, forecast accuracy, DSO, touchless processing and audit adjustments. Agree changed responsibilities and training with management and assess OR involvement where work organisation changes; any later use of AI for employee monitoring or employment decisions needs a separate AVG/GDPR and EU AI Act assessment.

by_role.title: FP&A Analyst
by_role.ambitious_version: Run a monthly rolling forecast for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, supported by weekly spending exceptions and peak-season contingency reviews. Give site leaders early options for agency cover, overtime and phased investment, and track whether approved actions improve forecast accuracy and shorten the close; use aggregated workforce data, involve HR and the OR where applicable, and assess EU AI Act requirements if the scope extends to individual employment decisions.

by_role.title: Accountant
by_role.ambitious_version: The two accountants run a close the three sites can use by working day four: a flex-versus-CAO labour bridge for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo while the pool is between 150 and 300, a tax position commercial can read before signing a foreign-principal contract, and a control log the auditor can re-perform from AFAS. The hours that leave the Excel bridges go into those decisions, which are the ones that move days to close and audit adjustments.

by_role.title: Credit and Collections Officer
by_role.ambitious_version: This officer runs order-to-cash for Noordhaven: reminder timing, credit holds inside the controller's ceiling, and a weekly note to Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo and to FP&A on why cash is late, split by damage, waiting time, missing proof, rate and surcharge. The new service is a cash-in forecast that moves when a promise changes, for the Finance Director's close. Demand for that forecast grows if it is cheap to keep: in the 2026 Onguard survey, 81% of Dutch finance and credit professionals explain DSO after the fact, and half plan cash-in no more than two weeks ahead. Smaller seasonal shippers, who today fall behind the large accounts, start to get a timely credit decision, while the officer's own calls stay on the disputed and the strategic accounts.

by_role.title: Controller
by_role.ambitious_version: The controller runs a close the Finance Director can sign in fewer days, and in the same cycle produces a forecast each site manager can use to change flex orders while the month is still open, plus a short financial note the works council can read. A weekly place-or-draw recommendation is on the Finance Director's desk in peak weeks, and a person still signs every movement at Rabobank. The controller is willing to be judged on days to close, forecast accuracy and audit adjustments.

by_role.title: Finance Director
by_role.ambitious_version: Aimed higher, this director would hold a 13-week cash and margin view that Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo use before they order flex or overtime, a credit decision on a logged fact sheet within one working day, and a weekly collection list aimed at the cash expected in the next six weeks. The board, Rabobank and the OR would take their figures from one pack that ties to AFAS, on a close that lands inside the days already agreed. The director's own time would sit on the forecast they will defend, the limits, the provisions, the surcharge and the few control changes that survive a quarter.
